questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires lose contact with the road. Your car rides on top of the water, called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent this is to drive slower in rain than in dry conditions.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using the brakes lightly. Pull off the road safely when you can.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Roads on bridges and overpasses can become icy when the rest of the road is dry. Bridges freeze before other roads and thaw out after them.

questions.question: In Kentucky, when can drivers use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals?

options.text: If the vehicle is not equipped with mechanical turn signals.
If the driver prefers to use hand signals.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, your car must have working mechanical turn signals. Hand signals are not allowed for passenger vehicles. Farm, construction, and animal-drawn vehicles are exceptions. Bicyclists may use hand signals.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where vehicles near you are located.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean?

options.text: Indicate no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs prohibiting the turn.

questions.question: There are oncoming cars on your left and parked cars on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When there are oncoming cars on your left and parked cars on your right, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If you drive alongside another vehicle on a multilane road, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.
Ask the other driver to slow down.
Speed up or slow down to move away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down to move away from them.
questions.explanation: Do not drive directly beside other vehicles on multilane roads. The other driver may not see you and could hit your car when changing lanes. Move ahead or drop back to stay out of their blind spot.

questions.question: A driver license is:

options.text: A right, not a privilege.
A privilege, not a right.
A requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is not a right. It is a privilege that you must earn and keep.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: At a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal about 100 feet before the turn.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal about 100 feet before the turn.
questions.explanation: Always signal 100 feet before turning. Keep your wheels straight ahead until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: Always stop before railroad tracks when:

options.text: You cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
The crossing is in a town with frequent trains.
You are carrying young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: Trains can come on any track at any time. Make sure your car clears the tracks completely before you stop.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to check for traffic.
Slowly pass stopped vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to check for traffic.
questions.explanation: At these locations, look to the left and right of your vehicle to see if anyone is coming into your path.

questions.question: Large trucks lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving through long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks accelerate slowly and lose speed going up hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to dangers ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful when turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars is still on the road. It mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: Adjust the driver's seat so you can see the pavement ____ in front of your vehicle.

options.text: 12 to 15 feet
12 to 15 inches
5 to 10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 feet
questions.explanation: Before driving, adjust your seat so you can see 12 to 15 feet ahead. Your chest should be 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel center. Your shoulders should be level with the top of the steering wheel.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a business or residential area?

options.text: 15 mph.
25 mph.
35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a business or residential area is 35 miles per hour. Follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: If you come to an intersection and cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Maintain your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop completely. Then inch forward until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your driving. Know how your medications affect you before driving.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all other vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and drive when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot turn in that direction. Come to a complete stop and wait for a green signal before proceeding.

questions.question: In bad weather, what should you do?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle in poor conditions.
